declaration.rationale: Necessary Dispatch native deliveries have observed arrival-to-FIFO waits up to 811 ns; all but at most 3 ns overlaps local service. One 1360 ns data transfer completes at 30280 ns after its delayed final packet. The later rank completion waits for status; distinguish a real delivery effect from a masked operator effect.
competing_explanations: Faster local service advances these same deliveries and propagates to needed operations
Queue reduction is masked by later status preparation, other outlets or fixed reordering
Changed feedback and packet paths change the actual critical object; compare new complete gates
declaration.retained_low_effect_reference: N2 physical FIFO waits are at most 81 ns in the auxiliary case; its actual final status has zero FIFO wait and 1 ns arrival-to-FIFO. No N2 service intervention without additional business-effect evidence.
declaration.caution: Effects apply to this existing 256-request normal reference, not the 1024-request discovery case or calibrated hardware

candidate_decisions.normal_reference: Retain as measured local network waiting with weak operator/segment effect; do not promote to a new measurement problem in this reference
candidate_decisions.discovery_case: Limited, not falsified: 1024-request packet membership and directed service effect were not measured
evidence: 811 ns arrival-to-FIFO wait overlaps local busy service apart from at most 3 ns; FIFO accounting exactly matches independent occupancy
One faster directed outlet reduces the reference maximum to 93 ns; complete contributions include both improvements and regressions

All 12 compared receiver/actual-last operator finishes advance only 8 ns; following expert and post-Combine compute are reviewed separately; the final necessary condition remains later status/local send completion
1024 long-prefix VOQ peak-window mean at the same outlet/phase is 46714.556 B versus 226342.996 B in the short segment; strength is prefix-sensitive
limits: Arrival-to-FIFO includes fixed allocation; busy overlap alone does not exclude simultaneous credit gating
Service intervention changes serialization, queueing and injection feedback jointly; not pure removable queue loss
No target-hardware calibration or discovery-scale causal claim

candidate_decisions.normal_reference: Retain as low-impact FIFO reference; no separate service run justified
candidate_decisions.discovery_case: Limited, not falsified: original 1024-request event lacks packet-level gate membership
evidence: Reference FIFO waits are at most 81 ns and fully overlap local service
Actual final incoming status from rank 86 has zero FIFO wait and 1 ns arrival-to-FIFO
Its receiver completion and later global gates remain controlled by status/local send completion; original discovery aggregate cannot identify a particular waiting status
limits: This does not prove every packet or larger-scale FIFO event is harmless

information_assessment.reason: Neither packet-verified normal reference demonstrates a material operator or successor-compute delay from the selected outlet; the larger discovery case remains unverified
what_is_not_concluded: A diagnostic algorithm has been evaluated
information_assessment.minimum_remaining_evidence: For the 1024-request discovery case: reproduce the original frozen graph, verify passive capture equivalence, identify actual selected-outlet packets and complete gates, then one directed service control if justified
